title: Best Adjustable Dumbbells UK
short: Adjustable dumbbells compared by weight range, adjustment mechanism and build quality, from beginner sets to serious home gym kit.
intro: A set of adjustable dumbbells replaces a whole rack of fixed weights in a fraction of the floor space, but the adjustment mechanism and weight range vary enormously between models. This guide compares dumbbells tested by Men's Fitness across exercises like presses, deadlifts, curls and farmer's carries.

products.name: 232 Adjustable Dumbbells
products.best_for: Buyers who want the smoothest, most premium adjustment experience
products.summary: Men's Fitness's top pick, with a seamless twist mechanism that cycles between weights instantly and no rattling of plates during lifts. Available in four colours with an optional hip-high stand, though the handle grip could be slightly better for high-intensity exercises.
pros: Slick, stylish aesthetic in four colours
cons: Handles could be grippier for high-intensity exercises

products.name: Personal Series Adjustable Dumbbell Pair
products.best_for: Experienced lifters who want maximum flexibility across 21 settings
products.summary: The best-in-test weight range at up to 34kg per dumbbell, with 21 different weight settings across the range. Men's Fitness found the slider selection system a breeze to use and the handles stayed comfortable throughout long workouts, though they're longer than most adjustable dumbbells and take up more space.
cons: Take up a fair amount of space
products.search: Primal Strength Personal Series Adjustable Dumbbells

products.name: Select-A-Weight Dumbbells
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong value with an easy adjustment dial
products.summary: Men's Fitness found these a breeze to use and pleasantly compact at 49.2cm long, the second smallest unit tested, calling them very good value. The iFit companion app has limited dedicated content and the 25kg max weight may not be enough for experienced lifters.
cons: 25kg max weight won't suit experienced lifters

products.name: 5kg-32.5kg Quick Select Adjustable Dumbbell
products.best_for: Buyers with limited space who still want to lift heavy
products.summary: The most space-efficient adjustable dumbbell Men's Fitness tested at just 42cm long, while still offering the second-heaviest max weight on test. The soft, textured handle grips securely, and the dock-and-dial adjustment system works smoothly, though it's relatively expensive.
pros: Wide resistance range for its size

products.name: SelectTech 552i Dumbbells
products.best_for: HIIT and explosive training where quick weight changes matter
products.key_spec: 2-24kg range, 15 increments, rubber and steel grip
products.summary: A rubber and steel grip well suited to explosive exercises, moving from 2kg to 24kg with a simple twist of the dial. Men's Fitness liked the JRNY app's on-demand strength classes, but noted the heavy use of plastic means they don't feel the most durable if dropped.
pros: JRNY app offers on-demand strength classes
cons: Heavy plastic use feels less durable if dropped

products.name: 24kg Adjustable Dumbbells
products.best_for: Buyers who want a genuinely good sub-£200 pair
products.summary: Sub-£200 dumbbells that Men's Fitness said surpassed expectations for value and functionality, with a smooth single-handed twist mechanism and a handy two-year warranty. Compact at 39 x 20 x 23cm, though there's a little rattle and the 24kg top end may be too light for stronger lifters.
cons: 24kg top end may be too light for some

products.name: AD80 80lb Adjustable Dumbbells
products.best_for: Buyers who want the toughest, most confidence-inspiring build
products.key_spec: 4.5-36.3kg range, 8 increments, dovetail changing mechanism, 1,000x drop guarantee
products.summary: A dovetail design creates a snug, rattle-free fit between plates and forms one of the most robust changing mechanisms Men's Fitness has used, backed by a 1,000x multi-angle drop-proof promise. Optional magnetic plates allow micro-adjustment, though it's one of the pricier options and extending the warranty costs extra.
pros: Useful range, fine-tunable with magnetic plates

products.name: Adjustable Dumbbell
products.best_for: Buyers just starting out who want a low-cost, no-frills option
products.summary: Men's Fitness found these undercut every other option on test by more than half, with a foolproof, robust adjusting mechanism and a slick, compact tray design. The weight range is aimed squarely at beginners, and you'll need to buy two separately to make a pair.
cons: Weight range aimed at beginners only
Must buy two individually for a pair

guide.q: What weight range do I actually need?
guide.a: Beginners are usually well served by a range up to around 20-25kg per dumbbell. Intermediate and experienced lifters doing heavier compound moves like squats or deadlifts benefit from a set that goes to 30kg or more, like the Primal Strength or Snode here.

guide.q: Dial, twist or slider adjustment: does it matter?
guide.a: All three can work well, but the number of increments and how quickly you can change weight both matter for keeping workout momentum, especially during supersets or drop sets. Dial and twist mechanisms, like the Nuobell and Braingain here, tend to be the fastest to operate one-handed.

guide.q: How much space do adjustable dumbbells actually save?
guide.a: A single pair of adjustable dumbbells can replace what would otherwise be 5-8 pairs of fixed dumbbells, which is a significant floor-space saving in a home gym. Compact models like the MuscleSquad here are worth prioritising if space is especially tight.

guide.q: Are cheaper adjustable dumbbells worth it?
guide.a: For beginners or anyone unsure how committed they'll be to home training, a budget option like the Amazon Basics or Braingain here is a sensible way to start without a large outlay. As strength and consistency build, many lifters upgrade to a set with a higher maximum weight and smoother mechanism.
